stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after espionage and affair scandal
stories.summary: Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, president and director after an investigation into affairs with a direct report and an alleged Chinese intelligence asset. The news wiped out roughly $1.4 trillion in market value.
stories.more: Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and had led it ever since, making the resignation one of the most abrupt CEO exits among major tech companies. The board, now chaired by Harvey Jones, opened the investigation after learning of the affairs, one of which involved a woman suspected of spying for China. Coverage describes the fallout as extending beyond Nvidia itself, given the company's central role in AI chip supply. It remains unclear what, if any, legal exposure Huang faces, and how the leadership change will affect Nvidia's AI strategy and partnerships going forward.

stories.title: Nvidia CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO after Huang's exit
stories.summary: Nvidia named longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO following Jensen Huang's resignation. Kress, who helped drive Nvidia's transformation into an AI powerhouse, now leads the company through the transition.
stories.more: Kress has served as Nvidia's chief financial officer for years and is credited with helping steer the company's finances through its rise as the dominant AI chip supplier. Her appointment as interim CEO came the same day the board announced Huang's resignation. Coverage focuses on her background and the question of whether she, or another candidate, will be named permanent CEO. No timeline for a permanent successor has been reported.

stories.title: Jensen Huang agrees to testify before Congress
stories.summary: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang agreed to testify before Congress after lawmakers threatened to subpoena him over the espionage and affair scandal that ended his tenure.
stories.more: The agreement follows Huang's resignation after Nvidia's board found he had affairs with a direct report and a woman suspected of spying for China. Several senior lawmakers had threatened a subpoena before Huang agreed to appear voluntarily. No date for the testimony was given in the report. The hearing is expected to probe both the alleged espionage angle and any implications for US chip export security.

stories.title: Trump suggests Apple's Tim Cook should succeed Huang at Nvidia
stories.summary: President Trump posted on Truth Social that Apple chairman Tim Cook is the only person who could replace ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
stories.more: The suggestion came shortly after Nvidia's board announced Huang's resignation and named CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Trump did not elaborate on why Cook would be suited to lead Nvidia, and there is no indication Cook or Nvidia's board are considering the move. The comment adds a political dimension to the already high-profile leadership shakeup at the world's most valuable chipmaker.

The report does not break down how much of the fund is earmarked specifically for AI versus other sectors, nor does it name specific portfolio targets. It is also unclear how the raise compares in timing to other large AI-focused funds closed this year.

stories.title: Fireworks AI breach exposed Notion customers' chat transcripts
stories.summary: A cyberattack on Fireworks AI let hackers access chat transcripts belonging to Notion customers, marking Fireworks' second data breach in as many months.
stories.more: The report identifies this as Fireworks AI's second breach in two months, though it does not detail how the earlier incident compared in scope. Notion apparently relies on Fireworks' infrastructure in a way that exposed customer chat transcripts to the attackers. The excerpt does not specify how many customers were affected, what data beyond transcripts was exposed, or what remediation steps either company has taken. It also leaves open whether the same vulnerability was exploited in both incidents.

stories.summary: Nine Korean startups spanning healthcare, fintech, energy, semiconductors and AI are competing for a place in TechCrunch Disrupt 2027's Startup Battlefield 200, aiming to expand into the US.
stories.more: The competing startups work across deep tech sectors rather than AI alone, though AI is listed among their focus areas. All nine are reportedly seeking to enter the US market, suggesting the competition is being used as a launchpad for international expansion. The report does not name the specific startups or detail selection criteria for the Battlefield 200. It is unclear how many total applicants are vying for the Korean slots.

stories.title: ElevenLabs launches Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live speech recognition models
stories.summary: ElevenLabs released Scribe v3 and Scribe v3 Live, speech recognition models that use conversational context to stop voice agents from cutting off callers mid-sentence. Benchmarks show it narrowly beats OpenAI, Google and Microsoft on accuracy.
stories.more: According to Artificial Analysis benchmarks cited in the report, Scribe v3 edges out rivals on transcription accuracy even through background noise and crosstalk. That accuracy comes at a cost: competitors like Microsoft and xAI run several times faster and charge roughly half the price. Scribe v3 Live is aimed specifically at voice agents, using conversational context to avoid interrupting callers. Pricing and availability details beyond the benchmark comparison were not specified.

stories.title: Google DeepMind releases AlphaGenome 2 for single-cell genomics
stories.summary: DeepMind unveiled AlphaGenome 2, which analyzes genetic variants at the level of individual cell types rather than bulk tissue. Trained on over 107 million cell profiles, it identifies nearly twice as many disease-relevant gene changes as its predecessor.
stories.more: The shift from bulk-tissue to single-cell-type resolution is meant to give researchers a finer-grained view of how genetic variants affect specific cells rather than averaged tissue samples. The model is available for noncommercial research use through an API, and Google plans to integrate it into its agentic platform, Antigravity. The report does not specify commercial licensing terms or a timeline for the Antigravity integration. It is unclear how the model performs on cell types underrepresented in its training data.

stories.title: Google, Samsung and partners launch $395 Gemini-powered smartglasses

The $395 starting price positions it as a mass-market product rather than a premium device. Details on battery life, camera specs and regional availability were not included in the excerpt.
